citations.review_text: This game is so badly optimized for anything other than a high end pc most of my time playing is waiting for the game to stop freezing and stuttering every 5 seconds or less.
It runs around 30-40 fps on my laptop with dips to below 30 sometimes. Im sure with a better pc it could be a great game.

The game is just not finished. It is not optimized, over bloated in file size, eats up a massive amount of resources and overall just feels like something that needed another year or two in development. Not at all what was advertised.

It may be a Stalker game, but I've played stalker mods on Arma that run smoother than this game. Not worth it unless you have a monster PC.

Been getting the itch for some STALKER as of late and been enjoying anomoly, especially the various modpacks available and after getting some PC upgrades I decided to see if I'd be able to enjoy STALKER 2 after updates have happened, but unfortunately I get the same FPS no matter the settings basically requiring frame generation to see anything higher than 50 FPS which sadly adds a very noticeable amount of input lag.
I really want to enjoy the game and support GSC as they've truly built something amazing here, but it just seems like it's more meant as a tech demo rather than a game meant to be played and enjoyed.

Really wish there was a middle option for reviews, since I want to give it a yes and no, but in it's current state I just can't recommend the game with it's lack of performance.

1,5 years after release it's still nowhere near where it should be to deliver an experience like the old games did.

Pros:
- It's Stalker: Atmospheric unique setting in a mysterious and thrilling open world
- sadly that's it

Cons:
- Performance is bad. It's unoptimized UE5 and eats hardware like it's nothing
- Localization: English only (and in this case Ukranian) is a poor trend
- AI/NPCs: Alife 2.0 promised at release is still, well, nowhere near where the old games were to make a friendly description
- Enemies see you like they have X-Ray vision and hit like aimbot - even through walls
- NPCs spawning right behind you
- Bullet sponge enemies
- Too many repetitive game mechanics (quests, stashes, ...)
- Often feels like a hiking simulator
- Shader compilation takes ages at every gamestart
- Mods can help, but modding UE5 requires mods being updated for every tiny patch the game gets. In consequence mods tend to stop being available
- Could go on with this list, but...

I really would like to enjoy this, because I loved the OG Stalker games back in the days, but all that really is making it hard for me.
I have some hopes for the upcoming engine upgrade regarding performance, and Cost of Hope (what a ironically perfect name) when it comes to bugs, glitches and so on, but I read that they plan on implementing better lighting, what probably results in worse performance, and I expect CoH to be mostly content related.

Performance wise I really would like to have options that result in way more FPS, even if it looks like garbage afterwards. In current situation most settings don't change anything in FPS, no matter if set to "low" or "high", and the other ones only have minor impact.

Maybe I'll give it another 1,5 years, or more..

Time and time again my character either runs on the spot or gets stuck on invisible objects even on flat ground. The enemy AI will also regularly attempt to shoot you through walls and floors. If there's anything which breaks immersion and kills the player, it's those two flaws.

I regret my purchase, especially with how expensive the game was.

Bought it 07/2026. Game is updated and content has been added since launch. I'm playing in veteran and i've sink too much hours in the old games and mods. 

I'm happy to have a new Stalker game, yet i don't like how it plays. I will mod it to death and probably have a lot of fun, but the base game is lacking. 16 hours in and it doesn't scratch the itch as much as playing the old anomaly mod does. I guess it's a okay buy on sale, but not full price. 

Why ? 

Stamina : biggest let down. Sure the old games had stamina, but they felt different. Here stamina feel like a hindrance for everything i'm trying to do. I spend more time chugging energy drinks than shooting at mutants. Which lead to the second point ... 

"Puzzles" : Stashes and objectives are (sometimes) hidden behind " " puzzles " " (for a lack of better word). Mostly they consist on jumping around. Lads, we're past 2020 - can't we do better ? Almost 20h in and i've spend 2/3 of my play time jumping around and chugging energy drinks. It's not fun or entertaining for me, i was expecting more - the old games were sometimes lacking in content but quests were far more interesting than "drink 5 galons of energy drink to bring me 2 fkng pebbles". 

Gunplay : Again, we're in 2026 and we have games like Tarkov (and other sims) that offers slow and intense gunplay with heavy gun customisation. I don't want Stalker to be more Tarkov, but somehow ... i do. Gunfights are boring and yes, ennemies do shoot you through terrain. I've been shot multiple times through vehicules (metals) and walls (inside buildings). It's easy enough to wait a corner for ennemies to slowy show their head and headshot them. Usually they can tank two bullets in Veteran. 

Mutants : since the gunplay is mid, fighting them isn't really fun. I've encoutered half the classic roster for now and nothing really interesting happened. I'll wait and see if the big boys bring some excitement but i doubt it. Anyways, it shouldn't be that way, i s…

The game is 40% fun, 60% frustrating. I'd still continue to play because I really love the gunfights, but I have to push through so much agonizing content in game. Let's see;

— AI is like Superman. They detect you really fast even if you stealth. They have x-ray vision. They can scent you like houndogs. They will shoot through walls. They have autobot headshot aim and will shoot you perfectly 100m away with a shotgun. 
— Game is so buggy. I lost my marbles trying to find artifacts, only to find out they can clip through walls/terrains. Sometimes important stuff you need won't spawn or clip through anything, you will even have a hard time getting items on boxes because the collision shoots stuff to the metaverse. 
— Sooooo many visual glitches. You'll see your screen flickering very often. You'll see things become blurry af. You'll see lighting twitching like mad. 
— Stare into the abyss on daylight and watch yourself get headshotted by an enemy npc in the dark bcz your flashlight feels like a mini-penlight. There's something fundamentally wrong with the darkness in game, it takes so long for your screen to adjust to the brightness of light and dark. Also, NPCs can accurately shoot and see you in the dark without any flashlights on. 
— This game is an unoptimized hell. You'll see memory leaks left and right, it'll randomly play at 5fps in your playthrough and you have to restart to fix it. Even DLSS can't save their game's mess. Honestly, even if an AI fps generator can't provide the game even an ounce of fps, you know it's bad. 

I still have a ton of hours to go through in this game, but it already has so maany issues in early game. Those stuff I listed apparently gets worse in later stages, especially on performance in populated areas so goodluck to me. 

To anyone who wishes to play and buy this, do it with precaution. The game can still be fun tbh it really did have potential, but the negatives can outweigh the good. This game really needs to be patched up bcz …

The game's immersion, environment and sound design is brilliant, the graphics are beautiful and over all the actual gun play is quite rewarding - however, this is totally blind sided by the AWFUL AI. They are given cheats, will beam you within seconds of spotting you and sometimes will begin firing through walls. 

It totally ruined the game for me as every conflict felt unfair. Bushes? Useless. Trees? Useless. Broken car? Useless in terms of cover. I found you're better off sprinting in circles to dodge bullets that duck behind cover. 

Until there's a mod that improves the AI, or there's some sort of update - don't bother buying the game. 

It reminds me of EFT, where shotgun scavs would head eyes you across the map.

Overrated? Yes.
Bad AI? Yes, they shoot through walls.
Janky movement? Yes.
Poorly optimized graphics and gameplay? YES.

I bought this at 30% off and I feel scammed.

Game is still a mess more than a year on from release. AI is awful, performance is terrible. World can be fun but loot balance sucks. You'll fight aimbotting wallhacking soldiers for 20 mins all for a pack of sausages and an energy drink.

citations.review_text:
This is my first S.T.A.L.K.E.R. game. I never played the original trilogy, so there is zero nostalgia influencing me here. I originally put about 15 hours into the PS5 Pro version before starting over on PC, and this is where the game really clicked.

The setting is wild. It takes place in “The Zone” which is a quarantined area surrounding Chornobyl. I haven’t read Roadside Picnic or watched Tarkovsky’s Stalker, but I’m familiar with their influence on the series, and it’s a sick premise for a game. Look them up to get a better idea. We’ll be here all day if I try.

Visually, the game is stunning, but the sound design might be even better. The Zone is eerie as hell. Sometimes the ambient audio alone is enough to unsettle you.

Immersive Mode is available at anytime and completely removes the HUD. No compass, icons, objective markers, nothing. Just the world. You actually have to look, listen and pull out your in-game tablet when needed. On an ultrawide OLED with headphones, it gets intense.

Gunplay is challenging but fair, exploration feels organic rather than like clearing 900 map icons, and the A-Life system allows NPCs to travel, fight, scavenge and die independently of you. I’ve witnessed things I thought were scripted that apparently just happened because I was there. That’s dope.

The character’s story and mission hasn’t really hooked me. It’s the setting. The factions, mysteries and history of the world your character inhabits are genuinely intriguing.

For me, this wasn’t a kick-back-and-lounge shooter. That’s what killed me trying to play on console. It demands attention and gives me some of the same vibes as Tarkov, Hunt: Showdown and Ready or Not, despite being a very different game.

Great gunplay, incredible atmosphere and sound, meaningful exploration and surprisingly effective horror. I restarted after 15 hours and somehow like it even more now. I look forward to seeing where this game goes. And with a major update coming on August 20th, I’d say this…

Restricted area, radiation storm, randomly scattered cans, unpredictable groups of travelers, weather, and distant howling mutant creatures - the environment is extremely immersive, The content is quite extensive. which are everywhere, the basic items are mostly food, drink, and bandages. If there's anything good, it usually has a jump rope, a special point, or a password door guarding it. The only way to teleport is between different camps. The rest can only be done on foot. Sometimes in the later stages, a single mission requires running a couple of kilometers. Even without carrying any weight, because the physical strength is quickly depleted, once it's gone, walking and returning becomes extremely slow. One can only wait in place... Additionally, from other survivors, I traded quite a lot of beverages. Because they can enhance endurance, speed of recovery, replenish the stamina bar, and are very helpful for running and long-distance travel. Although all my travels were spent drinking, until I got completely drunk.

In the modern day, is a jank game made in Ukraine still considered Slavjank, or is it just Eurojank now? Regardless, STALKER 2 is under the same level of jank as its predecessors even with a much prettier and stable engine. However, the ambition to make a game of this size despite the considerations of the ongoing Russo-Ukraine war is worth praise by itself, especially with the continued updates it's received.

I enjoyed my time overall in STALKER 2, but I felt that some design choices are very questionable even when compared to its predecessors, and the ending almost entirely soured me on the game as a whole. Below are some major complaints I have with the game.

[h3]GENERAL GAMEPLAY[/h3]

The A-Life system is notably neutered in comparison to the others. to the point where even [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3780670537]preserving their own life[/url] isn't a goal they follow, The spawning algorithm is also a bit broken in the current version, resulting in terrifying sights like [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3780671637]this one[/url].

This is probably the worst game in the series to fight mutants in. Many of them can stun-lock you with a knockdown attack, I think there is an unnecessary addition of psi damage on most mutant attacks (Snork jump attacks are the obvious example because they do so much damage even with [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3780671234]maximum physical protection[/url]), and Burers are so...♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Just absolutely awful design. Their shields making them immune to everything is especially obnoxious, and unlike in CoP THEY CAN STILL ATTACK WHILE IT'S UP.

[hr][/hr]

[h3]DIFFICULTY[/h3]

The difficulty balancing in this game is abysmal especially in comparison to other STALKER games. 

[url=https://www.reddit.com/r/stalker/comments/7fxvt5/what_do_difficulties_actually_change_in_stalker/]Here's[/url] the table from the STALKER reddit on the difficulty changes …

Huge fan of the STALKER franchise and had major hopes for this game. Credit where credit is due, this is an absolutely GORGEOUS game. I love the Artifacts, being able to see and hold them properly, I enjoy the storms and the detail to the weather, the detail to the weapons is cool. But the actual game itself is unplayable for me; screen tearing, jittering with each step, enemies who shoot through walls or get stuck in the floor and are incapable of getting out, duplicate NPCs who get stuck doing the triplet act of walking in circles... It simply is not worth trying to play until they push out a few more fixes.

The main issue is the horrible AI.  Waring factions will join together and hunt you down.
They will ignore all immediate threat and attack you.
Enemies with a shotgun will snipe you at 100 meters.
Enemies will attack you through the wall.
No Dash/ Evade skill- sucks when some enemies can kill you with a single blow.
During a few quests hostile NPC will keep re/spawning if not killed fast enough.
And the AI is just dumb as ♥♥♥♥ compared to it's predecessors.
Repair cost of items is just insane.
There are serveral bugs that have been here since day one.
Roughly two years have past and nothing has changed.
The world just seems empty, dead and boring. Nothing has any kind of meaning. Decision carry no weight.
I'll just storm tropper this ♥♥♥♥♥ and call it a day. I'm utterly disappointed
if enemies stop shooting you through concrete walls.... i will give it a thumbs up.

This game has some amazing aspects and a lot of potential, but at this time it's an absolute mess. There are some absurd design decisions, such as high mutant health regardless of difficulty setting, astronomical upgrade/repair costs, being unable to sell gear that's not in good condition, the stupid fast travel system, quest items, consumables and bullets weight, stamina regeneration tied to that carry weight system etc. I'm well aware that developers intention is to make the game more challenging and realistic, but having to carry insane amount of bullets due to super tanky enemies and then carry weight restricting looting to pay for those bullets, repairs/upgrades and new gear is just dumb, overall the balancing is all over the place. 

Then theres the bugs, artifacts spawning underground, some anomalies being invicible, enemies spawning right in front of you, infinitely spawning enemies, a bug where the game spawned like 30 burers in a few meter radius, enemies shooting/spotting you through the walls while your bullets can't go through bushes, quests breaking if you stray away from a certain path and so on. 

Games optimization is still awful, it looks very good [i] sometimes [/i] but not nearly good enough to justify the performance. There's also a problem with visual glitches, loading times and rebuilding shader cache every time you launch the game. 

Propably 3 hours of my playtime was trying to fix the game by modding it, but a lot of mods are outdated and some break the game even more. 

The game has some good things, the atmosphere is great, gunplay and sound design are amazing and those combined make this really immersive. But with all the negatives outshining the positives this game is probably one of the most frustrating experiences I've ever had with a video game. Not recommended.

- The gunplay feels great. Every single weapon I used had good feedback, from recoil to sound to damage. Quick-swapping attachments is also cool and adds an extra layer of mobility during intense gunfights.
- The atmosphere is great, some places had me staring at the scenery for a while, while others almost had me shaking with anxiety. The settlements, while mostly decrepit, gave a soothing sense of comfort.
- The graphics are very nice c:
- The dialogue is funny and witty, especially if played in Ukrainian. 

The bad:
- After a while, everything feels the same. The guns feel the same, the armor, the loot, the encounters, even the scenery. Previous titles had a distinct feel to every area. Here, however, everything feels recycled over and over again.
- A-Life is non-existent. It still boggles me how a 2007 game (or earlier, F.E.A.R., for example) had more complex and smart AI than this.
- Loot is plentiful, and your worst enemy is encumberance, instead of having to ration your bandages, food, or ammo.
- Instead of making mutants actually dangerous, they're just bullet sponges, and unloading 120 5.45 bullets into 3 bloodsuckers isn't a problem, since I have freaking 400 of those from 10min of walking around, and I need to lose some weight anyways.

- The story is not engaging at all. At a certain point I realized I had no idea what I was even doing. There's no tangible sense of mystery or wonder. I just found myself getting the same kick out of this game as with Far Cry or Borderlands. Just run around and shoot stuff.

Just can't recommend it to anyone who is genuinely interested in what the series is known for. 
Sadly, Stalker 2 is just another mediocre open-world RPG, another Skyrim, another Fallout 4. 
Past the many technical issues: severe bugs unfixed this long after release, horrible performance, and astonishingly bad lighting everywhere, GSC just forgot what made Stalker so great. 

Stalker was good for its AI & world simulation for emergent stories & a living world, fast and tight yet fair combat, well-designed and visually interesting areas, RPG mechanics rewarding good use of items & upgrades, and many memorable encounters & sequences.
Stalker was not good because of graphics, or story, or GOOD voice acting, or having immersive animations for everything you do, or having the biggest open world everrr.

Unfortunately, the developers decided to focus on exactly these things at the cost of everything else.
There has been absolutely no iteration on the game's best mechanics and gameplay loops, in fact, much has regressed. What we got was a mediocre Unreal Engine 5 remake, not a true sequel to finally take the series out of the 00's.

# **STALKER 2 Review (51.6 Hours | Veteran Difficulty)**

I put **51.6 hours** into STALKER 2 on **Veteran** and made it to the final Monolith missions. Honestly, I don't think I'll even finish it.

I refunded the game at launch because of how rough it was. After hearing it had improved, I bought the **Ultimate Edition** and gave it another shot. It has improved, but I still walked away more frustrated than impressed.

The biggest problem isn't that STALKER 2 is hard.
It's that it **doesn't respect your time**.

Instead of feeling like I was surviving the Zone, I felt like I was maintaining it.

## The Good

* Unreal Engine 5 looks fantastic.
* Incredible atmosphere.
* Great sound design.
* Guns sound and feel satisfying.
* Seeing old locations and familiar faces like **Beard, Nimble, Sultan and Scar** was a nice nostalgia hit.
* The foundation for an amazing game is absolutely there.

### Veteran difficulty becomes a job

By the end of the game:

* My fully upgraded armour was constantly in the red.
* My favourite weapons were always close to breaking.
* Repairs cost a fortune.
* I spent more time maintaining equipment than fighting.

I wasn't carrying every ammo type because I was prepared.

I was carrying them because I'd pick up dead enemies' guns, use them until they nearly broke, throw them away, then repeat to avoid destroying my own upgraded weapons.

### Carry weight is the real final boss

I filled every artefact slot with carry-weight bonuses.
Reduced weapon weight.
Upgraded everything I could.
Still overloaded.

Every trip became:

* Throw away vodka, food and bandages.
* Unload every weapon before looting.
* Drag guns onto the ground.
* Hit "Take All."
* Walk back to a safe zone at a snail's pace.
* Spend nearly every coupon repairing gear.
* Organize my stash.
* Walk all the way back again...
* ...only to realise it's now night because I forgot to sleep.

### Combat kept interrupting itself

Combat should be the best part.

Instead it becam…

This game has some amazing aspects and a lot of potential, but at this time it's an absolute mess. There are some absurd design decisions, such as high mutant health regardless of difficulty setting, astronomical upgrade/repair costs, being unable to sell gear that's not in good condition, the stupid fast travel system, quest items, consumables and bullets weight, stamina regeneration tied to that carry weight system etc. I'm well aware that developers intention is to make the game more challenging and realistic, but having to carry insane amount of bullets due to super tanky enemies and then carry weight restricting looting to pay for those bullets, repairs/upgrades and new gear is just dumb, overall the balancing is all over the place. 

Then theres the bugs, artifacts spawning underground, some anomalies being invicible, enemies spawning right in front of you, infinitely spawning enemies, a bug where the game spawned like 30 burers in a few meter radius, enemies shooting/spotting you through the walls while your bullets can't go through bushes, quests breaking if you stray away from a certain path and so on. 

Games optimization is still awful, it looks very good [i] sometimes [/i] but not nearly good enough to justify the performance. There's also a problem with visual glitches, loading times and rebuilding shader cache every time you launch the game. 

Propably 3 hours of my playtime was trying to fix the game by modding it, but a lot of mods are outdated and some break the game even more. 

The game has some good things, the atmosphere is great, gunplay and sound design are amazing and those combined make this really immersive. But with all the negatives outshining the positives this game is probably one of the most frustrating experiences I've ever had with a video game. Not recommended.

I’ll start with something simple so people who want to buy this game don’t fall into the same trap I did. The starting area is great — the game begins really strong. But the longer you play, the more obvious it becomes that the whole thing is held together with duct tape and the mindset of “we’ll fix it later.” It felt like the first ~20 hours were genuinely polished, but after that the game kept getting worse and worse. Not in terms of story — I couldn’t even bring myself to finish it — but technically. More and more quests started breaking, bugging out, or becoming impossible to complete.

What’s the biggest problem with the game? Simply put: boredom.

The gameplay loop looks like this: you get a mission 1.4 km away (0.86 miles for the freedom people), and you run there. Sounds normal, right? Except it’s literally just running. Nothing happens on the way. Sprint + energy drink to instantly restore stamina, over and over again. The A-Life system that was heavily advertised simply doesn’t work, and nothing meaningful has been done about it. Almost every update so far has just been fixing basic issues that never should have made it into the final release in the first place, with an occasional new weapon thrown in to keep players happy.

I have a love-hate relationship with this game.

I got hooked on the series after playing Shadow of Chernobyl, and when STALKER 2 is at its best, it's one of the most immersive games I've played. The Zone is spectacularly detailed, atmospheric, and absolutely massive. Unfortunately, I also think it's a little too big for its own good. I spent many hours simply sprinting across huge distances with very little happening, as if the developers were spread too thin. Side missions often feel more like a checklist of chores than meaningful extensions of the world.

The main story does have some genuinely breathtaking moments, memorable characters, with some epic cutscenes. Even so, the pacing, especially in the middle of the game, drags a lot more than I'd like.

The balancing also still needs work. The older games were difficult but, apart from Clear Sky, I usually felt my deaths were fair. Here, enemies often have laser accuracy, can spot you from absurd distances, and getting sniped by an enemy you can't see with a shotgun just isn't fun.

Performance is another major issue. The developers have made impressive improvements through patches, and with the upcoming engine update I'm hopeful things will continue to improve. Even so, the game's current performance is hard to excuse for a modern AAA release. There are still areas where I struggle to maintain 50 FPS on hardware that really shouldn't be having problems.

Despite all of that, I still can't help but recommend it.

Few games create an atmosphere as compelling as The Zone, and when everything is working right, I tend to let go of my frustrations and I'm reminded why I keep returning. It's a deeply flawed game, but one with a world unlike anything else. So if you do try it, just understand what you're getting into.

- Broken Endgame Missions: The late-game difficulty spikes are almost impossible. Fights against the Granite squad and Scar feel fundamentally untested. The absolute worst offender is the Granite Squad arena section where you are dropped into a room with zero cover against a firing squad. You take fire from enemies that can two-shot you from afar while others pepper you in CQB, leaving you with nowhere to run.

The Verdict
I cannot recommend S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 in its unmodded state. Even with mods to fix the economy and bugs, the endgame missions are such an unbalanced slog that it feels like the game actively doesn't want you to finish it. I highly recommend a modded playthrough…
